key_insight: Teaching a model to predict actions alongside video can weaken its existing understanding of how language relates to visual events. SWAM investigates how data and supervision can preserve that alignment during action learning.
problem_solved: World action models need to predict both video and actions from language instructions, but action training may disrupt language–video alignment learned during video pretraining.
method: Study language–video alignment when action learning is introduced into a pretrained video model.
Investigate data and supervision design for maintaining cross-modal alignment.
The supplied abstract is truncated, so specific dataset details, training mechanisms, and results are unavailable.
impact: This work highlights cross-modal alignment as an important consideration when extending video models to action prediction. It could guide training-data and supervision choices, although the provided excerpt does not establish performance gains.

paper_title: SWAM: Scaling World Action Models with Cross-Modal Alignment
